name: Website uptime watchdog with incident tracking

nodes.name: Read Sites
nodes.notes:
The Sites tab needs these columns:
Site Name | URL | Expected Status | Expected Keyword | Max Response ms | Fail Threshold | Alert Email | Active

Blank Expected Status means any 2xx passes.
Blank Expected Keyword skips the content check.
Blank Max Response ms means 5000.
Blank Fail Threshold means 2 checks in a row.
Alert Email is optional and accepts a comma separated list.
Write no in Active to pause a site without deleting it.

nodes.name: Decide Transition
nodes.notes:
A site must fail its threshold number of checks in a row before it is called DOWN, which is what filters out one-off blips. Recovery is immediate on the first healthy check.
While an incident stays open a reminder is sent every 6 hours rather than every 10 minutes.

nodes.name: Save State
nodes.notes:
The Site State tab needs these columns, left empty for the workflow to fill:
Site URL | Site Name | State | Problem Count | Down Since | Last Alert At | Last Checked | Last Status Code | Last Response ms | Last Reason

Rows are matched on Site URL, so there is always one row per site and this doubles as a heartbeat showing the monitor itself ran.

nodes.name: Log Incident History
nodes.notes:
The Incident History tab needs these columns:
Site Name | Site URL | Incident Type | Started At | Recovered At | Duration Minutes | Last Reason

One row is written per closed incident, at the moment a site recovers, so total downtime is known.

nodes.name: Send Error Alert
nodes.notes:
This branch only fires if the workflow itself crashes.
Open workflow settings and set Error Workflow to this same workflow, otherwise it never runs.

parameters.content:
## 1. Load the sites
Every 10 minutes the Sites tab is read. Paused and blank rows are dropped, URLs are normalised and duplicates removed, then sites are checked one at a time so response time is measured honestly.

## 2. Check each site
One real request per site with a 15 second timeout and redirects followed. A failed request does not stop the loop. The result is judged on status code, keyword and response time, then the site's previous state is loaded.

## 3. Decide, then alert
A site is only called DOWN after several failed checks in a row, so a single blip stays quiet, but it returns to UP on the first healthy check. Alerts go out on a new incident, on recovery, and as a reminder every 6 hours.

## 4. Save and log
The current state is written on every pass, which doubles as a heartbeat for the monitor itself. When a site recovers, one incident row is closed off with its start time and total downtime.

## 5. Daily digest
Each morning Slack gets a summary: how many sites are up, slow or down, incidents closed in the last 24 hours, total downtime and the slowest sites.

## 6. Crash alerts
If the workflow itself fails, this branch posts the failed node and a link to the execution. Set Error Workflow in workflow settings to this workflow to switch it on.

# Website uptime watchdog with incident tracking

Checks every site listed in a Google Sheet every 10 minutes, tracks each as UP, SLOW or DOWN, and alerts your team only when the state genuinely changes. Catches wrong status codes, missing keywords, timeouts, DNS failures, expired certificates and slow responses.

### How it works
1. The Sites tab is read, paused and duplicate rows dropped, and sites are checked one at a time so response times stay accurate.
2. Each site gets one real request with a 15 second timeout, judged on status code, expected keyword and response time.
3. A site is only called DOWN after several failed checks in a row, which stops a single blip paging anyone. Recovery is immediate on the first healthy check.
4. Alerts go to Slack on a new incident, on recovery with total downtime, and every 6 hours while an incident stays open. An optional per-site email is alerted too.
5. State is written on every pass, so the sheet doubles as a heartbeat. When a site recovers, one incident row is closed with its duration.
6. Each morning a digest goes to Slack with how many sites are up, incidents closed in the last day, total downtime and the slowest sites.
7. A separate branch alerts you if the workflow itself crashes.

### Setup
1. Create one spreadsheet with three tabs: Sites, Site State and Incident History. The columns are in the notes on the Read Sites, Save State and Log Incident History nodes.
2. Connect Google Sheets, Slack and Gmail, then replace YOUR_GOOGLE_SHEET_ID and YOUR_SLACK_CHANNEL_ID.
3. In workflow settings set Error Workflow to this same workflow, check the timezone, then activate.

### Customization
Tune Fail Threshold and Max Response ms per site in the sheet, no editing needed.
